newsitem.title: Singapore: Singapore names date for general elections.
newsitem.headline: Singapore names date for general elections.

text.p: Singapore will vote in general elections on January 2, the government said on Monday.
Prime Minister Goh Chok Tong claimed victory earlier in the day for his People's Action Party (PAP) after opposition parties decided to contest only 36 of the 83 seats in parliament.
In the last elections in 1991, the PAP won 77 of the 81 seats in parliament. Redrawn constituency boundaries have added two more seats this time.
The Election Commission said voting day, a Thursday rather than the usual Saturday, would be a public holiday with schools used as voting centres.

The January 2 date gives the minimum period of nine days for campaigning following the close of nominations on Monday. The PAP normally goes for the minimum to give the opposition the least chance of mounting a sustained campaign.
